relevance_note: Case report of a girl with a de novo heterozygous TNFAIP3 frameshift ('a heterozygous mutation (c.436_437deTC) in the TNFAIP3 gene') plus a literature table of 29 earlier patients with TNFAIP3 variants.
method_note: Read the whole paper (case report with a literature table). Rows built by a Python script from my own reading; the script parsed Table 1 cells directly from the Markdown and every table-derived value was checked against the table by eye. SCOPE/LABELS: the case patient is labelled 'patient' (rule 5; she is also Table 1 row 30, 'This case', which is not given a separate row). Her parents were Sanger-tested negative and get rows 'father of patient' and 'mother of patient' (no variant rows, checklist all not reported). The 29 previously published patients in Table 1 rows 1-29 have no individual label column (the Pedigree column holds family labels), so they are labelled 'Table 1 row k' (rule 3). BLANK CELLS: per rule 6, empty Pedigree, Mutation location and References cells in continuation rows were recorded as not reported. The layout suggests these rows continue the family/variant/reference above (consistent with the stated '29 cases ... from 13 families'), but the table does not print it per row, so family_label, variant and source_reference_in_review are not reported for those rows; they still get a variant row with variant_original_string 'not reported' because the table title ties every row to TNFAIP3. Cells '\' and '/' are undefined and treated as not reported. Onset 'Unknow' (row 19) recorded as not reported. CHECKLIST CHOICES: table 'Fever' was not mapped to 'recurrent fever' (not stated as recurrent); only row 13 ('intermittent fever', Diagnosis column) and the patient ('recurrent fever') are observed. 'oral mucosa, genital ulcer' read as oral mucosal and genital ulcers. Stomatitis, perianal ulcer, GI symptoms, bloody stool, colonic perforation and pharyngitis were not mapped to checklist items. Skin abscess, acne, aquatic keratoderma, urticaria and inflammatory skin swelling were counted as skin lesions; cerebral palsy/autism (row 20) and encephalopathy (row 25) as CNS involvement; scleritis as ocular inflammation; pericardial effusion as serositis. Patient: ANA 1:100 taken as positive (titer reported, no interpretation given); negative neurological examination taken as excluding CNS involvement; ocular symptom denials and 'no conjunctival congestion' did not exclude ocular inflammation (narrow vs broad). Patient age at last evaluation and at diagnosis not recorded: the only age given is at admission (2 years 3 months), while follow-up continued to January 25, 2021; country not stated (hospital is in Xinjiang). Vital status 'alive' inferred from the reexamination on January 25, 2021. CONTRADICTIONS: (1) Table 1 lists genital ulcers for this case, but the text says the parents denied vulvar ulcer and no vulvar abnormality was noted; both rows emitted, checklist genital ulcers not reported. (2) Table 1 lists nonspecific rash for this case, but the examination found 'no skin rash'; both rows emitted, skin lesions not reported. (3) The variant is printed as 'c.436-437deTC' (abstract), 'c.436_437deTC' (case report text and Table 1) and 'c.436_437delTC' (Figure 4 legend); the case-report text form was recorded. (4) The text says 'this case and the 48 cases reported so far are summarized in Table 1', but Table 1 has 29 earlier cases plus this case, matching 'a total of 30 cases, including this case' (used for n_patients_reported). (5) Family 1 is cited to Shigemura et al [14], whose reference title names a C243Y mutation, while p.Cys243Tyr is listed for Family 3 (no reference printed). (6) Families 2 and 12 carry the same variant (c.252delC p.Trp85GlyfsX11) with members of identical onset age and sex (11 yr F, 9 mo F), cited to Kadowaki [4] and Ohnishi [15]: possibly the same people reported twice; not merged. (7) Table rows 9 and 10 are textually identical, so their spans are identical. Row 1 'Other medical history' reads 'syndrome, 5 relapses after hormone withdrawal' (apparently truncated). The patient's joint pain was denied at admission but knee pain, synovitis and effusion were later documented (and effusion/thickened synovium were already on admission ultrasound); arthritis treated as observed. Minor: two different VitB12 values and 'IL-6 65.5 mg/L' are printed in the admission labs (not used).

her symptoms had not been alleviated after the oral administration of iron dextran

symptomatic treatments including oral administration of prednisone (12.5 mg/d) and iron supplement were performed, and repeated infection was no longer observed in the child. The dose of prednisone was reduced gradually to 10 mg/d.

the treatment regimen was adjusted to oral prednisone (12.5 mg/dose, 2 doses/d) and subcutaneous injection of recombinant human type II tumor necrosis factor receptor-antibody Fc fusion protein (rhTNFR:Fc; 12.5 mg/wk)

the treatment with iron supplement was stopped. The limbs’ activities were normal, the inflammatory indicators were ESR 11 mm/h, PCT 0.02 ng/mL, CRP 12 mg/L, and IL-6 8 pg/mL, and TNF was in the normal range. The prednisone dose was reduced to 7.5 mg/d, while the dose of rhTNFR:Fc was not changed.
